newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Islamist party to boycott elections.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Islamist party to boycott elections.

text.p: Pakistan's fundamentalist Islamist Jamaat-i-Islami party has decided to boycott national elections set for February 3, state radio said on Sunday.
It quoted Jamaat chief Qazi Hussain Ahmad as saying his party's central body had taken the decision because the present caretaker government had failed to stem corruption.
The Jamaat has been in the forefront of a campaign against ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto but has not not done well in past elections.
President Farooq Leghari dismissed Bhutto's three-year-old government on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
No corruption charges have been formally brought against any politician yet.
